description: HydroStream v2.1 is a Python pipeline for joining historical and current Environment Agency water-quality CSV exports into analysis-ready tables. Its own documentation sets a validated source transition at 13 October 2025, applies one schema and unit policy, preserves qualified measurements and emits CSV or Parquet with optional statistics and quality reports. Zenodo archives the version 2.1 code and describes testing on a frozen 2000 to July 2026 source snapshot; large raw Environment Agency files are not included there. The repository supplies command-line and notebook workflows, but users must obtain source exports from the official Water Quality Explorer and preserve download dates to reproduce a release. The repository states CC BY 4.0 for its materials; the Environment Agency observations have Open Government Licence 3.0 attribution terms. Coverage is England water-quality sampling points and chosen analytes, not a network hydraulic or treatment-plant process trace. A modeller can prepare quality boundary conditions or compare environmental effects, subject to spatial matching. The live archive can change after the frozen test cut. No raw export, archive or pipeline was run. The related catalogue record covers hydraulic network examples; HydroStream supplies environmental observations, not those network files.
